Welcome to Planet. We believe in using space to help life on Earth.

Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company all rolled into one.

Customers and users across the globe use Planet's data to develop new technologies, drive revenue, power research, and solve our world’s toughest obstacles.

As we control every component of hardware design, manufacturing, data processing, and software engineering, our office is a truly inspiring mix of experts from a variety of domains.

We have a people-centric approach toward culture and community and we strive to iterate in a way that puts our team members first and prepares our company for growth. Join Planet and be a part of our mission to change the way people see the world.

Planet is a global company with employees working remotely world wide and joining us from offices in San Francisco, Washington DC, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, and The Netherlands.

We are looking for a Senior Product Designer to design, prototype, and launch CivGov and Commercial Solutions and define how users interact with and derive insights from Planet’s satellite Earth Observation (EO) data.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between Planet’s platform capabilities and valuable customer outcomes. With a relentless focus on the user, you will define user profiles, establish jobs-to-be-done, and design end-to-end user flows for high-value market opportunities. You will collaborate closely with Product and Engineering to decompose these workflows into scalable, reusable UX building blocks, ultimately crafting cohesive, customer-centric solutions.

This is a full-time, hybrid role which will require you to work from our Berlin or Haarlem office 3 days per week.

· Product Design Leadership: Drive the end-to-end design process, from initial discovery and user research to prototyping and high-fidelity execution.

· Discovery & Validation: Lead user research and prototype testing to validate high-value use cases within CivGov and Commercial ensuring all development is grounded in validated user needs.

· User-Centric Goal Setting: Define clear objectives based on user discovery (e.g., identifying success criteria for a CivGov compliance officer) to drive meaningful outcomes.

· Design & Architecture: Architect intuitive interfaces that translate complex geospatial data into actionable insights, establishing reusable interaction patterns and components for Planet’s solutions.

· Cross-Functional Strategy: Partner with product and engineering to ensure top-tier design quality; facilitate cross-team collaboration to align on ambiguous problem spaces and bridge the gap between technical capability and customer value.

· Design Culture: Actively contribute to building and elevating Planet’s design culture.

Kleines Team, kurze Wege, echte Eigenverantwortung. Kein Investment-Board. Kein Design-by-Committee.

In my previous roles, product teams always consisted of a product manager, a designer, and ~4-5 engineers. This may sound familiar to you! The product manager briefs the designer who then designs. After designing, mocks are handed to the engineers.
We take a more principled approach here at Ashby. If you've been designing software enough, you'll realize in actuality, design is required in varying degrees on each project.

Sometimes in the past, I'd be asked to design yet another settings page, when really all that was needed was an engineer to reuse existing components and just follow some documentation I had written. Other times, I felt I should effectively be the product manager and own a project from beginning to end.

In these latter cases, it made sense that I was even the one providing project updates and managing resources rather than constantly being pinged by a separate product manager.
This principled approach is now what we do here, and it is part of what has allowed Ashby to take down incumbents in multiple verticals all at once. We don't settle for the status quo—we actively resist reversion to the mean.

The belief is not that design is unimportant, but rather that it should be owned by the product team collectively, not solely by a group of full-time designers who happen to have the job title.
The design department’s job at Ashby is not to make every single design decision but to equip our entire product team to make better decisions themselves, as well as edit decisions that PMs/Engineers choose to make. That, while tackling the biggest design challenges ourselves.
Separate from design, you may also be excited by the fact that we maintain a near seed-stage-like culture with fuzzy lines between functional roles, as much autonomy as you can handle, and a focus on IC-work with an almost-no-meeting culture. We're looking for a designer who decides with evidence. Most design roles stop at the handover. This one does not. You will design a part of the product, form a view about what should change, build the experiment that tests it, and read the results yourself. If you have ever shipped a redesign and never really found out whether it worked, this is the opposite of that.
You will sit inside one product delivery leadership team, working closely with the person accountable for that part of the business and with the engineers building it – not off to one side taking requests. And you will not be doing it alone: you join a group of Product Designers across the company who work the same way and hold each other's standards.
English is our working language. German matters here too: you will be designing flows that German-speaking neighbours read.

Design experiences that fit how people already live. Our product mirrors real neighbourhood life. Your job is to design flows and screens that feel natural to someone standing on their doorstep with one hand on their phone, not to add features because we can.
Frame the real problem before solving it. Take a vague ask, find the actual question underneath it, and make it explainable. A well framed problem to solve is half the battle.
Run the experiment, and read it honestly . Design a testable change, get it instrumented properly, and analyse the outcome with our data team. That includes reporting the tests that did not work, which is most of them, and saying what you would do differently.
Talk to neighbours. Experiments tell you what happened, not what people needed. You will spend real time with the people who use this, because you cannot A/B test your way to understanding somebody.
Direct AI, and spend your judgment where it counts. AI produces a lot of our first-pass design. You will brief it, push back on it, and hold the quality bar, so your own hours go to the thinking a model cannot do. Polish goes where it changes behaviour, not onto every surface.
Argue for cutting things. Adding is easy. You will help decide what earns its place and what should be removed, and be willing to make the case for less.

You practice design, and you are very comfortable with numbers. You might come from an analyst background and bring a love of design and design thinking, or vice versa.
You have technical know-how. You need to be able to construct the pipelines and dashboards yourself, use our experimentation platform, and our design system tooling.
You get your own numbers. Whether through SQL, AI-assisted querying, or both, you do not wait for someone else to pull data for you.
You have run experiments end to end. Hypothesis, design, instrumentation, analysis, decision. Not just handing a mockup to someone who tested it later.
You care about craft and are attentive to details. You can tell the difference between good enough and actually good and you design experiences people do not have to think about.
You use AI as a tool already or want to. This role allows you to have more control and impact through both design and analysis, but to do this well you'll need to leverage (and at times extend) our AI enablement stack.
You present your work clearly, defend your decisions when challenged, and are comfortable in front of a crowd.

Warum LPE Immobilien? Die Hausverwaltung ist der unterschätzteste Beruf Deutschlands: Kein anderer entscheidet so unmittelbar darüber, wie Menschen wohnen. Trotzdem gilt der Hausverwalter bis heute als Buchhalter mit Schlüsselbund. Wir wollen das ändern, und Software ist dafür einer unserer zentralen Hebel.
Mit lpeOS bauen wir die Systeme, mit denen wir selbst jeden Tag arbeiten: das Kundenportal für unsere Eigentümer, KI-Agenten, die eigenständig Aufgaben übernehmen, und das Verwaltercockpit als Arbeitsumgebung unserer Verwalter. Wir digitalisieren unsere eigenen Prozesse, um die Arbeit unserer Verwalter jeden Tag ein Stück besser zu machen, mit dem Anspruch, die Branche zu revolutionieren.
Für Design ist das ein seltener Ausgangspunkt: Kaum eine Branche wurde von moderner Software so lange übersehen. Für diese Berufe hat noch nie jemand ernsthaft gestaltet. Du wärst die erste Design-Person in unserem neuen Produktteam und baust Design-System und Designprozess mit auf.
Was dich bei uns erwartet – Deine Aufgaben Wir arbeiten als ein Team von Product Engineers , manche technischer, manche gestalterischer. Du wärst die gestalterischste Person, arbeitest aber im selben Repository und Rhythmus wie alle anderen. Was du gestaltest, ist meist wenige Wochen später live.
Du verantwortest den Designprozess von Anfang bis Ende : Du führst Interviews mit Verwaltern und Eigentümern, verdichtest die Erkenntnisse zu Konzepten und gestaltest daraus Interfaces für Kundenportal und Verwaltercockpit. Deine Kolleginnen, Kollegen und Kunden sind direkt erreichbar, Feedback bekommst du auf kurzem und direktem Weg.
Deine Designs bleiben nicht in Figma : Mit KI-gestützter Entwicklung (React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui) bringst du sie selbst ins Frontend und setzt Teil-Features, teils auch ganze Features, gemeinsam mit dem Team um. Du musst kein Programmierer sein, aber du willst, dass deine Arbeit im Produkt landet, und legst dafür selbst Hand an.
Ein besonderes Feld ist Design für KI-Agenten : Du gestaltest Interaktionsmuster für Workflows, in denen Agenten Aufgaben übernehmen. Wo braucht der Nutzer Kontrolle, wo Transparenz? Muster, für die es noch kaum Vorbilder gibt.
Was du mitbringen solltest 2 bis 5 Jahre Erfahrung im Produktdesign, gern mit B2B-Software oder komplexen Workflows.
Ein Portfolio mit 2 bis 3 Case Studies, die deinen Weg von der Nutzerfrage bis zum ausgelieferten Interface zeigen: Deine Denkweise interessiert uns mehr als die Menge an Screens.
Sicherer Umgang mit Figma, von Wireframes über klickbare Prototypen bis zur Komponentenbibliothek.
Erfahrung mit qualitativem Research: Interviews führen, Erkenntnisse verdichten, Annahmen mit Usability-Tests prüfen.
Gespür für Interaction Design und Informationsarchitektur in datenreichen Anwendungen.
Gute bis sehr gute Praxis mit KI-gestützter Entwicklung (z. B. Claude Code, Cursor, v0): Du bringst Teil-Features oder ganze Features selbst in den Code.
Solide Grundlagen in HTML und CSS, JavaScript ist ein Plus.
Deutschkenntnisse mindestens auf B2-Niveau.
Du erfüllst nicht alle Punkte? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Talent und Lernkurve zählen bei uns mehr als Jahreszahlen im Lebenslauf.
Was wir dir bieten Eine seltene Ausgangslage. Wir bauen Software für ein Geschäftsmodell, das bereits funktioniert, und wissen, dass sie gebraucht wird. Du erlebst aus nächster Nähe, wie sich eine ganze Branche neu erfindet, und gestaltest das aktiv mit.
Echter Impact. Alles, was du gestaltest, kommt bei unseren Verwaltern, Eigentümern und Kunden direkt zum Einsatz.
Eine Branche von innen kennenlernen. Die Immobilienwirtschaft ist einer der größten Märkte Deutschlands und steht erst am Anfang ihrer Digitalisierung. Du lernst sie dort kennen, wo die Entscheidungen fallen.
Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Produktverantwortlichen. Kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen und jemand, der sich Zeit für deine Fragen nimmt.
Mentoring und Weiterentwicklung. Wohin du dich entwickeln willst, Richtung UX Engineering oder Produktverantwortung, besprechen wir offen und regelmäßig. Mentoring ist bei uns in alle Richtungen möglich.
Ehrliches Feedback. Sofort und in beide Richtungen.
Die richtigen Werkzeuge. Premium-Hardware, cloudbasierte Tools, aktuelles KI-Tooling, papierlos. Wenn dir etwas fehlt, um besser zu arbeiten, bekommst du es.
Perspektive. Diese Stelle ist so gebaut, dass sie mit dir und mit lpeOS wächst.
